report:
**Conclusion: no.** The best current evidence does **not** show that saw palmetto *alone* improves urinary symptoms from benign prostatic enlargement more than placebo in the longer term.

A 2023 Cochrane systematic review—designed to weigh all randomized evidence—concluded that saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) alone provides “little to no benefits.” It defined long-term follow-up as beyond 12 months; evidence for combination herbal products was more uncertain, so this should not be interpreted as support for saw palmetto itself.  
https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001423_serenoa-repens-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia

This conclusion is consistent with the major one-year, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled trial: saw palmetto was not superior to placebo for either urinary symptoms or objective BPH measures.  
https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa053085

Why the belief persists: older, generally smaller trials sometimes suggested benefit, but later and better-controlled trials did not confirm it. A prior evidence review specifically concluded that Serenoa repens was no more effective than placebo, while appearing relatively safe.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20941857/

Saw palmetto may be reasonably well tolerated, but “safe” is not the same as effective. It also should not substitute for assessment of bothersome or worsening urinary symptoms, which can have causes other than BPH and may need proven treatments.
